observation: Water jet appears discretized into a repeating stack of pancake-like blobs rather than a continuous pressurized fan-shaped stream; suggests per-frame emission stepping or low-res meshing/particle conversion.
expected_behavior: A continuous, coherent jet/sheet that breaks up into ligaments and droplets with non-periodic spacing, especially at 2–3 m/s pressurized rupture.
actual_behavior: Regularly spaced, similar-sized lobes/segments along the jet path; limited ligament formation and micro-spray; floor impact lacks energetic splash crown/ejecta.
recommended_fix: Increase inflow temporal sampling to reduce emission stepping (Flow > Sampling Substeps: 2 → 6–8). Increase solver max substeps/time steps (e.g., 4 → 6–8) and keep adaptive time stepping on. If mesh looks chunky, adjust liquid mesh generation smoothing/particle radius; optionally raise domain resolution (96 → 128) if bake time allows.
analysis_notes: Regularly spaced jet lobes are characteristic of per-frame/under-sampled emission or insufficient substeps, especially for fast inflows. Resolution 96 may be adequate but time stepping and mesh settings can still produce quantized segments.
